dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For matrices A and B, this is the real number 4·(n:ℝ)²·(θ⁻¹)²·Gmin·LocalDef003(A)·LocalDef003(B), with the products associated from left to right.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For X : Fin r → Fin s → ℝ, it forms each nonnegative row sum Σ_j ‖X(i,j)‖, takes their finite maximum in NNReal with empty maximum equal to 0, and returns the underlying real number. Thus it is the maximum absolute row-sum norm, with value 0 when there are no rows.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the two nonnegative factors measuring A and B separately on both sides of the inequality.

binders: m, n, and q are arbitrary natural numbers.
θ, gmin, and Gmin are arbitrary real numbers.
A is an arbitrary real m×n matrix, represented as A : Fin m → Fin n → ℝ.
B is an arbitrary real n×q matrix, represented as B : Fin n → Fin q → ℝ.
mathematical_definitions: For X : Fin r → Fin s → ℝ, define ‖X‖row = max_{i ∈ Fin r} Σ_{j ∈ Fin s} ‖X(i,j)‖, where the finite maximum over no rows is defined to be 0.
For real entries, the entry norm is the standard nonnegative real norm, equivalently absolute value.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every choice of natural dimensions m, n, q, every pair of real matrices A of size m×n and B of size n×q, and all real parameters θ, Gmin, and gmin, if θ is at least 1 and 0 ≤ Gmin ≤ gmin, then four times n squared times Gmin divided by θ squared, multiplied by the maximum absolute row-sum norms of A and B, is at most four times n squared times gmin divided by θ, multiplied by the same two norms.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement is an implication: whenever any of 1 ≤ θ, 0 ≤ Gmin, or Gmin ≤ gmin fails, it is true vacuously and asserts no scalar inequality for that choice of parameters.
The assumption θ ≥ 1 makes θ positive and nonzero, although Lean's real inverse is defined even at zero.
The assumptions imply gmin ≥ 0, but no strict positivity is required for either Gmin or gmin.
No dimension is required to be positive. In particular, n=0 makes the coefficient (n:ℝ)² zero and the conclusion reduces to 0 ≤ 0.
If m=0 then ‖A‖row=0; if q=0 then every row sum of B is zero and ‖B‖row=0. These cases also reduce the conclusion to 0 ≤ 0.
Zero matrices, or any matrix with zero maximum row-sum norm, likewise make both sides zero.
The matrix quantity is specifically the maximum absolute row-sum norm, not the spectral norm, Frobenius norm, or a norm of the matrix product AB.
No matrix product AB, approximation error, computed result, algorithm, rounding operation, or floating-point quantity is present in the proposition.
There are no existential quantifiers or witness dependencies.
The conclusion is non-strict and compares only two scalar products sharing the same nonnegative coefficient and matrix-norm factors.
